# Follow up: Airtable & Discord

**Pattern:** Drip Sequence · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers auto-responders work end to end across Airtable and Discord.

It moves through 11 working steps, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Segment Audience
3. Step 1 — Welcome (Discord)
4. Tag for Slow Nurture
5. Wait Before Step 2
6. Converted Already?
7. Step 2 — Value Nudge (Discord)
8. Mark Converted — Stop Drip
9. Wait Before Final Step
10. Step 3 — Final Offer (Discord)
11. Update Drip Status

## Why it exists

Doing auto-responders work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Segment Audience → Step 1 — Welcome (Discord) → Tag for Slow Nurture → Wait Before Step 2 → Converted Already? → Step 2 — Value Nudge (Discord) → Mark Converted — Stop Drip → Wait Before Final Step → Step 3 — Final Offer (Discord) → Update Drip Status

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Discord aligned by hand for auto-responders
- Auto-responders sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Airtable
- Auto-responders work where "Segment Audience" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Auto-responders work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Discord in step for auto-responders, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Airtable or Discord call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 11 nodes in this auto-responders build
- The pause before Airtable is durable — a auto-responders run survives a restart
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 11 nodes for auto-responders before wiring Airtable
- 11 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for auto-responders

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Discord webhook URL.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every step checks 'Converted Already?' before sending — a drip campaign that keeps emailing someone who already bought is the fastest way to burn trust. The Wait node's durable resume state (via `webhookId`) is what lets a multi-day wait survive an n8n restart instead of being held only in memory.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a 4th drip step with its own wait/exit-check pair.
2. Manually flip a test record's status to 'converted' mid-drip and confirm the ladder stops sending.
3. Shorten the wait durations so the full ladder runs in minutes instead of days, for testing.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your auto-responders process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
auto-responders payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
